title: Do not trust a long-running control after treatment/control boundaries drift mid-test
scenario: A 21-day Amazon Ads experiment launched with clean treatment/control routing. Mid-test, shared automation and a bulk negative change altered the control boundary, but the final readout still asks whether treatment won based on the original launch design.

mid_test_changes.detail: automation began harvesting a broad-match route into the control campaign that can reach a treatment query family
a bulk edit removed one control-side negative used to isolate the treatment query family

forbidden_behaviors: Treat launch-time control integrity as proof that the control remained clean for all 21 days.
Declare the treatment a causal winner without evaluating the day-9 and day-12 boundary changes.
Ignore newly introduced query reachability or changed negative routing because the control settings were clean at launch.
required_observations: Control integrity is a time-varying property and must be re-verified after material routing, automation, keyword/target, migration or negative changes.
The launch snapshot is stale after the day-9/day-12 scope changes and cannot validate the full experiment window.
The treatment lift may be reported descriptively, but causal confidence must be downgraded until the affected interval is reconciled, segmented, or the experiment is rerun with verified boundaries.

rubric.requirement: Detect that treatment/control isolation drifted after launch and invalidate launch-only integrity evidence.
Use dated boundary evidence and the mid-test change timeline rather than assuming static scope.
Hold, redesign, segment, or require manual review instead of action-safe rollout.
